rik: Heads-up: canary run on TP stacks showed a ~2.2x all-reduce tail latency increase when seq_len > 1024. Captured traces and a small repro. Suspect kernel selection + message fragmentation.
anita: ugh, can you paste the trace snippet? ring vs tree numbers?
rik: quick paste from the trace (trimmed):
```
step=allreduce tensor=tp_grad shard=0 msg_size=65536 ops=512 -> ring=2.8ms tree=1.9ms
step=allreduce tensor=tp_grad shard=0 msg_size=131072 ops=256 -> ring=3.6ms tree=2.0ms
step=allreduce tensor=tp_grad shard=0 msg_size=524288 ops=64  -> ring=8.4ms tree=6.0ms
notes: when messages are fragmented (~64k chunks) ring latencies blow up and we see poor overlap with compute.
```
anita: hmm tree looks strictly better for middle sizes here. Why is kernel_selector choosing ring?
jia: our autoswitch heuristic recently changed thresholds to prefer ring for <1MB because of earlier microbenchmarks. Might be the change that regressed this workload.
oliver: i ran the repro locally with `--tp=4 --seq-len=2048 --kv-delta=true` and got the same. Raw timeline shows many tiny allreduces interleaved with small kernels, so comm/compute overlap is minimal.
oliver: timeline snippet:
```
[compute] 0.0-1.2ms exec kernelA
[comm]    1.2-4.8ms allreduce(msg=64KB)
[compute] 4.8-6.0ms exec kernelB
[comm]    6.0-9.6ms allreduce(msg=64KB)
```
rik: that's the heart of it — KV cache + kv-delta sends create lots of fragmented messages (many 64KB chunks). The kernel selector biases toward ring for many small msgs which increases per-message overhead vs a tree/flat algorithm. Also our streaming scheduler isn't coalescing these deltas early enough.
anita: two paths: (1) tweak kernel_selector thresholds to pick tree for 32-256KB on TP, or (2) change batching heuristic to coalesce kv-deltas into fewer bigger packets before allreduce.
jia: +1 to batching change — it's lower-risk and benefits more workloads. But selector tweak is faster to patch in the short term.
perfbot: perf-regression-detect: job=tp-canary branch=main -> commit=7f3a4c reg=+22% tail-latency (p95) for tp-allreduce-seqlen-2048
oliver: repro command I used: `./run_tp_test --tp=4 --batch=1 --seq=2048 --kv-delta --profile=nvtx --out=trace.json`
jia: quick experiment: disabling kernel_autoswitch on my machine (force tree) dropped p95 from 12.8ms -> 6.1ms for the heavy seq run.
rik: good. let's do both: short-term force tree for kv-delta path and open an issue to improve batching/coalesce in the kernel that feeds allreduce.
anita: created issue #3241: "TP: allreduce fragmentation - kernel selector + batching heuristic" and assigned to @oliver for batching and @anita for selector patch. link: https://redwood/issue/3241
oliver: I'll push a micropatch to prefer tree for msg_size in [32KB, 512KB] for tp paths and add a runtime flag to toggle. canary after that.
rik: also note we should add a microbenchmark: run allreduce with interleaved compute to measure overlap effect. Add to perf CI.
jia: adding test to ci/perf: tp_allreduce_overlap_{32k,64k,128k,512k}.sh
anita: ok. follow-up: if KV cache fragmentation is the main cause we should also consider increasing kv-flush-coalesce window (default 8 -> 32) and measure unit-cost impact.
oliver: will iterate. thanks all :thumbsup:
perfbot: note: regression alert snoozed (24h) pending canary results"
